newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Elton John to perform at Hong Kong handover.
newsitem.headline: Elton John to perform at Hong Kong handover.

text.p: British pop legend Elton John will ring out the changes in Hong Kong in June, performing two concerts to mark the colony's historic handover to China.
"He is coming to Hong Kong on the last weekend of the handover," Peter Randall, head of public relations at the Hong Kong Tourist Association, told Reuters.

The 49-year-old singer and songwriter, as famous for songs such as "Rocket Man" and "Crocodile Rock" as for his feather and sequin stage outfits, is the first big-name entertainer to confirm he will perform at the handover.
Organisers said they hope 40,000 people will pack Hong Kong stadium for each of the shows on June 28 and 29.
Governor Chris Patten, an avid music lover, is said to be a big fan. He invited John to lunch at Government House in 1993.

The British flag will be lowered for the last time in Hong Kong at midnight on June 30, marking the end of more than a century and a half of colonial rule over the wealthy, vibrant community of 6.3 million people.
China's red flag will then be hoisted.

John's songs are extremely popular in China. But authorities in Beijing are said to have objected several years ago when the idea was floated of staging an Elton John concert within the walls of the old imperial Forbidden City.
Hong Kong plans to spend HK$233 million (US$30 million) on glitzy ceremonies to mark the handover.
